name: Pupil Dilation
description: Analyzes pupil response and dilation patterns
mechanism:
This method analyzes pupil dilation dynamics for deepfake detection:

1. **Pupil Tracking**: Precise pupil boundaries are tracked per frame using circular Hough transform or ellipse fitting. Pupil diameter is measured relative to iris diameter (to normalize for distance/zoom changes). The pupil-to-iris ratio temporal signal is extracted.

2. **Lighting-Pupil Correlation**: Pupil diameter should inversely correlate with ambient light level — brighter environment → smaller pupils. The method measures scene luminance and checks the pupil-light correlation. In deepfakes, generated pupil sizes may not respond to scene illumination changes.

3. **Dilation Dynamics**: Pupil dilation/constriction follows specific temporal dynamics: constriction is faster (~0.5s) than dilation (~1s), with characteristic latency (~250ms). The method verifies that observed pupil changes follow these physiological dynamics. AI-generated pupils may show instantaneous or non-physiological size changes.

4. **Bilateral Consistency**: Both pupils should maintain nearly equal sizes (anisocoria < 1mm in normal conditions). The method tracks left-right pupil size difference. Deepfakes frequently produce different pupil sizes in left and right eyes because each eye is generated independently.

5. **Pupil Shape Assessment**: Real pupils are circular (round pupil margin) under normal conditions. Slight elliptical deformation occurs only at extreme gaze angles. The method checks pupil shape — AI generators may produce irregularly shaped pupils, non-circular boundaries, or pupils that change shape between frames. The combined pupil analysis provides a physiological authenticity assessment.
parameters:
Analysis type: sensor
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through pupil dilation analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Matern, F. et al. (2019). Exploiting Visual Artifacts to Expose Deepfakes. WACVW.
